body:
Conclusion: the integration should expect Ordarium's dedicated cursor-rejection error — `InvalidCursorError` (@ordarium/core), error `code === "INVALID_CURSOR"`, message "The change cursor is not a valid durable position; refusing to guess a resume point". It fails closed; it is not a generic ledger failure.

Which cursor: the "observation cursor" is the durable resume position returned by the state change feed (`StateChangeFeed.changes()` / `StateStore.changes()`, ORD-BOOT-0). Core types describe it as "incremental observation of committed state revisions after a durable position" and `StateChangePage.cursor` as an "opaque, filter-independent durable position of the last delivered change" that a consumer keeps across restarts. It is rejected in two ways, both yielding the same error: (a) it cannot be decoded/validated (not base64url `{"c":"<digits>"}`, non-safe-integer, < 0), and (b) it is numerically ahead of the ledger's global high-water mark (foreign/restored/replaced ledger).

Decision basis (local, no peer escalation needed):
1. Pinned line is Ordarium 1.3.1 — package.json, pnpm-workspace.yaml overrides, and the installed artifacts (node_modules/@ordarium/core, /ledger-sqlite) all read 1.3.1.
2. In that pinned artifact, `errors.js`/`errors.d.ts` define `InvalidCursorError` with code `INVALID_CURSOR` and state explicitly: "A caller-supplied change-feed cursor could not be decoded as a durable position (ORD-BOOT-0). Distinct from LEDGER_CORRUPT: this is invalid caller input, not damaged ledger content, and it fails closed instead of silently restarting from the beginning of the feed." It is exported via `@ordarium/core` index.
3. Both ledger implementations throw it on this surface: the in-memory ledger in core `ledger.js` (4 decode-rejection sites plus the high-water check) and the reference `@ordarium/ledger-sqlite` (`changes()` high-water check ~line 393 and the four decode-rejection throws ~lines 776–787).
4. The only locally conflicting source is docs/engineering/10-legacy-error-codes.md, which says the 1.2.0 line reported "a generic ledger failure rather than a dedicated cursor-rejection error" and marks itself "superseded — void for the current pinned line". Because the conflict is settled by explicit supersession plus version scope (1.2.0 legacy register vs the 1.3.1 pin), the legacy doc is not co-applicable; the two sources never govern the same proposition.

What it is not, for disambiguation: not `LEDGER_CORRUPT` (damaged ledger content — the sqlite ledger's operation/list/history cursor decoders use `LedgerCorruptError`, a different surface, and the core docs explicitly separate the two); not `LEDGER_CAPABILITY_REQUIRED` (that fires from `StateStore.changes()` when the ledger declares no `stateChangeFeed` at all, before any cursor is interpreted); not `LEDGER_BUSY`/transient.

Integration handling implied: Palimpsest's single classification point (src/effects/errors.ts) matches only `UncertainOperationError`/`OperationBusyError`/`SimulatedProcessCrash` as transient and `LedgerBusyError`/`StateRevisionConflictError` as retry-safe. `InvalidCursorError` matches none, so it must surface terminally with no retry and no re-mapping, and callers must branch on `instanceof InvalidCursorError`/`code`, never parse raw messages (G2-A07).
